entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-2020-C2-Deriv-Kennan-03
entry.itemBody: Compared to over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives that are not cleared, the credit risk of exchange-traded derivatives is most likely:

answerFeedback.39206ac0-72d1-4993-9ce3-1ca400a1711b: Incorrect because derivative exchanges require collateral on deposit upon inception and during the life of a trade in order to minimize counterparty credit risk. This deposit is paid by each counterparty via a financial intermediary to the exchange, which then provides a guarantee against counterparty default, whereas OTC (over-the-counter) instruments have less transparency, usually involve more counterparty risk. Therefore, compared to OTC derivatives that are not cleared, the credit risk of exchange-traded derivatives is lower, not higher.
answerFeedback.410fcfc5-fa12-442d-9f78-2c1911b6dd01: Correct because derivative exchanges require collateral on deposit upon inception and during the life of a trade in order to minimize counterparty credit risk. This deposit is paid by each counterparty via a financial intermediary to the exchange, which then provides a guarantee against counterparty default, whereas OTC (over-the-counter) instruments have less transparency, usually involve more counterparty risk. Therefore, compared to OTC derivatives that are not cleared, the credit risk of exchange-traded derivatives is lower.
answerFeedback.88864cfe-5c82-45f2-b94b-764592c06e6c: Incorrect because derivative exchanges require collateral on deposit upon inception and during the life of a trade in order to minimize counterparty credit risk. This deposit is paid by each counterparty via a financial intermediary to the exchange, which then provides a guarantee against counterparty default, whereas OTC (over-the-counter) instruments have less transparency, usually involve more counterparty risk. Therefore, compared to OTC derivatives that are not cleared, the credit risk of exchange-traded derivatives is lower, not the same.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Bangaruswamy-01
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements is most accurate?

answerFeedback.58fd9cc2-eda7-4c00-a1f9-b365768b1907: Correct because other derivative underlyings include weather, cryptocurrencies, and longevity, all of which can influence the financial performance of various market participants. Therefore, longevity is an example of an underlying of a derivative.
answerFeedback.bab2c1ec-6fe8-49d4-a164-8739137f0cda: Incorrect because a distinct derivative contract, such as a derivative on a stock or bond, is an example of a stand-alone derivative. An embedded derivative is a derivative within an underlying, such as a callable, puttable, or convertible bond. Therefore, convertible bond is not a stand-alone derivative, but an embedded derivative.
answerFeedback.f019421e-05b8-4e29-88ef-49e5c3a1e885: Incorrect because a derivative does not directly pass through the returns of the underlying but transforms the performance of the underlying.

choices.itemBody: A. Longevity is an example of an underlying of a derivative
B. A convertible bond is an example of a stand-alone derivative
C. Derivatives directly pass through the returns of the underlying

entry.title: ITEM_2019BDeriv01EWL10U1
entry.itemBody: Derivatives derive their performance from:

answerFeedback.0efe7193-de5c-40ca-9c26-61d936d0d67d: Incorrect because derivatives are subject to the risk of default. Forward contracts are subject to default. This also applies to swaps, where either party can default but only one party can default at a particular time. While a credit derivative provides protection… against a specific credit loss, it does not eliminate the risk of default.
answerFeedback.186c1f60-4145-4467-85c9-b2062f8ce840: Correct because the most common definition of a derivative is a financial instrument that derives its performance from the performance of the underlying asset.
answerFeedback.82f0c590-2be9-4ecc-95f7-ed8074be51ec: Incorrect because the transformation of performance for the case of derivatives is a critical, factor distinguishing derivatives from mutual funds and exchange-traded funds and some other straight pass-through instruments.

choices.itemBody: A. the performance of the underlying asset.
B. eliminating the risk of counterparty default.
C. the straight pass-through performance of the underlying.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-05207
entry.itemBody: Compared to over-the-counter (OTC) derivative markets, exchange-traded derivative markets most likely have greater:

answerFeedback.2e3f2db3-cb25-42ad-99de-b87506a6bd57: Incorrect because exchange-traded derivatives are standardized, whereas OTC derivatives are customized. Therefore, exchange-traded derivatives markets have lower customization than OTC derivatives markets.
answerFeedback.618a0304-cc0a-4cef-a2e5-ff8e98fb8ecd: Incorrect because the OTC markets for derivatives will remain considerably more flexible than the exchange-listed markets. Therefore, exchange-traded derivatives markets have lower level of flexibility than OTC derivatives markets.
answerFeedback.e4b3e4a2-9e98-4253-8cb8-71cc9321f4de: Correct because many transactions in OTC markets will retain a degree of privacy with lower transparency. In contrast, exchange markets are said to have transparency, which means that full information on all transactions is disclosed to exchanges and regulatory bodies. Therefore, exchange-traded derivatives markets have greater transparency than OTC derivatives markets.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Berlinicke-06
entry.itemBody: Which of the following derivative underlyings is an example of a soft commodity?

answerFeedback.0a048ee5-6cb1-4170-9602-d44005a04b6d: Correct because soft commodities are agricultural products, such as cattle and corn, and hard commodities are natural resources, such as crude oil and metals. Also, crude oil, soybeans, copper, and gold are all commodities. Commodities are considered either 'hard' (those mined, such as copper, or extracted, such as oil) or 'soft' (those grown over a period of time, such as livestock, grains, and cash crops, such as coffee).
answerFeedback.66c7cbb0-bf9b-49c8-b608-4a363aa3fc5d: Incorrect because, despite its physical (liquid) nature, crude oil is categorized as a hard commodity since it is a natural resource. Soft commodities are agricultural products, such as cattle and corn, and hard commodities are natural resources, such as crude oil and metals.
answerFeedback.de321bee-dc19-4be1-a03b-4ad353dca507: Incorrect because gold is a metal and hence a hard commodity. Soft commodities are agricultural products, such as cattle and corn, and hard commodities are natural resources, such as crude oil and metals. Also, crude oil, soybeans, copper, and gold are all commodities. Commodities are considered either 'hard' (those mined, such as copper, or extracted, such as oil) or 'soft' (those grown over a period of time, such as livestock, grains, and cash crops, such as coffee).

entry.body:
Montau AG is a German capital goods producer that manufactures its products domestically and delivers its products to clients globally. Montau’s global sales manager shares the following draft commercial contract with his Treasury team:

Montau AG Commercial Export Contract

Contract Date: [Today]
Goods Seller: Montau AG, Frankfurt, Germany
Goods Buyer: Jeon Inc., Seoul, Korea
Description of Goods: A-Series Laser Cutting Machine
Quantity: One
Delivery Terms: Freight on Board (FOB), Busan Korea with all shipping, tax and delivery costs payable by Goods Buyer
Delivery Date: [75 Days from Contract Date]
Payment Terms: 100% of Contract Price payable by Goods Buyer to Good Seller on Delivery Date
Contract Price: KRW650,000,000

Montau AG’s Treasury manager is tasked with addressing the financial risk of this prospective transaction.
entry.title: Vignette
CFA2374-s004-Q6

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A 75-day timing difference exists between the commercial contract date and the delivery date when Montau AG is paid for the machine in KRW. A is true but does not explain why the use of a derivative is preferable to a spot market transaction. If as in C Montau were to sell the KRW it receives and buy EUR in a spot market transaction on the delivery date, it would be exposed to unfavorable changes in the KRW/EUR exchange rate over the 75-day period. A derivative contract in which the underlying KRW/EUR forward rate is agreed today and exchanged on the delivery date allows Montau to hedge or offset the EUR value of the future KRW payment. The derivative is therefore a more suitable contract to address the financial risk of the commercial transaction than a spot market sale of KRW.

entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements best describes why Montau AG should consider a derivative rather than a spot market transaction to manage the financial risk of this commercial contract?

choices.itemBody: A. Montau AG is selling a machine at a contract price in KRW and incurs costs based in EUR.
B. Montau AG faces a 75-day timing difference between the commercial contract date and the delivery date when Montau AG is paid for the machine in KRW.
C. Montau AG is unable to sell KRW today in order to offset the contract price of machinery delivered to Jeon Inc.

entry.title: CFA2374-s004-Q7

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The derivative best suited to hedge Montau’s financial risk is a firm commitment derivative in which a pre-determined amount is exchanged at settlement. The derivative underlying should be currencies, specifically the sale of KRW at a fixed EUR price in the future to offset or hedge the financial risk of the commercial contract. The machine price referenced under B is not considered an underlying, and C hedges the opposite of Montau’s underlying exposure.

entry.itemBody: Which of the following types of derivative and underlyings are best suited to hedge Montau’s financial risk under the commercial transaction?

choices.itemBody: A. Montau AG should consider a firm commitment derivative with currency as an underlying, specifically the sale of KRW at a fixed EUR price.
B. Montau AG should consider a contingent claim derivative with the price of the machine as its underlying, specifically an A-series laser cutting machine.
C. Montau AG should consider a contingent claim derivative with currency as an underlying, specifically the sale of EUR at a fixed KRW price.

entry.title: CFA2374-s004-Q8

feedback.neutral: C is correct as per the following diagram:

entry.itemBody: Identify A, B, and C in the correct order in the following diagram, as in Exhibit 1, for the derivative to hedge Montau's financial risk under the commercial transaction.

choices.itemBody: A. A: Financial intermediary, B: KRW650,000,000, C: Fixed EUR amount
B. A: Jeon Inc., B: KRW650,000,000, C: Fixed EUR amount
C. A: Financial intermediary, B: Fixed EUR amount, C: KRW650,000,000.

entry.title: CFA2374-s004-Q9

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The OTC market is most appropriate for Montau, as OTC contracts may be customized to match Montau’s desired risk exposure profile. This is important to end users seeking to hedge a specific underlying exposure based upon non-standard terms. Montau would be unlikely to find an ETD contract under B that matches the exact size and maturity date of its desired hedge, which also makes C incorrect.

entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about the most appropriate derivative market to hedge Montau AG’s financial risk under the commercial contract is most accurate?

choices.itemBody: A. The OTC market is most appropriate for Montau, as it is able to customize the contract to match its desired risk exposure profile.
B. The ETD market is most appropriate for Montau, as it offers a standardized and transparent contract to match its desired risk exposure profile.
C. Both the ETD and OTC markets are appropriate for Montau AG to hedge its financial risk under the transaction, so it should choose the market with the best price.

entry.title: CFA2374-s004-Q10

feedback.neutral: B is correct. In a centrally cleared OTC derivative contract, the central counterparty becomes the counterparty in all contracts and assumes the credit risk associated with individual derivative contracts. A is likely incorrect because the CCP takes actions to ensure that it can fulfill its obligations to its counterparties. C is incorrect because the CCP inserts itself between parties with opposite positions.

entry.itemBody: If Montau enters into a centrally cleared derivative contract on the OTC market, which of the following statements about credit risk associated with the derivative is most likely correct?

choices.itemBody: A. Montau faces credit risk associated with the possibility that its counterparty to the contract may not fulfill its contractual obligation.
B. Montau poses a credit risk to its counterparty because it may fail to fulfill its contractual obligation.
C. Montau poses a credit risk to a derivative contract end user holding a contract with the opposite features of Montau’s.

entry.title: ITEM_20170601014
entry.itemBody: A derivative can best be described as a financial instrument that:

answerFeedback.9816586a-7315-4e32-9230-60a3b14d7a3d: Incorrect. A derivative transforms the performance of the underlying asset rather than passing through the returns of the underlying asset.
answerFeedback.db15928f-b844-481a-8200-a2e49a5281d7: Incorrect. A derivative transforms the performance of the underlying asset rather than duplicating the performance of the underlying asset.
answerFeedback.e8ea618a-ce5e-4677-bb02-090f2375b816: Correct. The best characterization of a derivative is that it typically transforms the underlying asset’s performance.

choices.itemBody: C. passes through the underlying asset’s returns.

entry.title: ITEM_20170601016
entry.itemBody: Which of the following derivatives is least likely to be classified as a contingent claim?

answerFeedback.6b7ab2a4-b936-4a4a-bc6f-92c53848bf6d: Correct. A futures contract is classified as a forward commitment in which the buyer undertakes to purchase the underlying asset from the seller at a later date and at a price agreed on by the two parties when the contract is initiated.
answerFeedback.bddf1ccb-99f8-4115-ae1e-be999ad5ea54: Incorrect. A credit default swap is a contingent claim in which the credit protection seller provides protection to the credit protection buyer against the credit risk of a third party.
answerFeedback.da81bd23-171b-46cc-a3e6-a2d06736af59: Incorrect. A call option contract is a contingent claim in which the buyer of the option has a right to purchase the underlying asset at a fixed price on or before a pre-specified expiration date.

entry.title: ITEM_20170601020
entry.itemBody: In contrast to over-the-counter options, futures contracts most likely:

answerFeedback.0da0cb78-bbaa-4519-9a8b-0950d5841666: Correct. Over-the-counter options are exposed to default risk, but futures contracts are standardized transactions that take place on futures exchanges and are not exposed to default risk.
answerFeedback.883065a6-a77e-4c1c-9cd9-494b9f73f841: Incorrect. Futures contracts are commitments, but options represent a right.
answerFeedback.d7072120-102b-4be9-a890-e83df41be91d: Incorrect. Futures contracts are not private; they are standardized instruments that trade on organized exchanges.

choices.itemBody: A. are not exposed to default risk.
C. represent a right rather than a commitment.

entry.title: ITEM_20170601037
entry.itemBody: Which of these is best classified as a forward commitment?

answerFeedback.3398561d-f3fd-42db-8249-315e790a6610: Incorrect. A call option is an example of a contingent claim.
answerFeedback.6ff11456-74e3-4963-886a-22f3e114eb3f: Correct. A swap agreement is equivalent to a series of forward agreements, which can be described as forward commitments.
answerFeedback.fa26943a-396f-470f-8dea-46a5dba48d5b: Incorrect. A convertible bond does not meet the definition of a forward commitment.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Glover-01
entry.itemBody: Which of the following derivative contracts is best described as a contingent claim?

answerFeedback.bb5d512a-4911-4588-87f8-3363a3cd737e: Correct because another type of derivative is a contingent claim, in which one of the counterparties determines whether and when the trade will settle. An option is the primary contingent claim.
answerFeedback.bd5f35ac-397b-4244-952b-8dbaa3a0e0cd: Incorrect because derivative contracts can be classified as either firm commitments or contingent claims. Firm commitments include forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps involving a periodic exchange of cash flows and an option is the primary contingent claim.
answerFeedback.e09a5552-9b29-43cc-949a-6f4ce120a1a5: Incorrect because derivative contracts can be classified as either firm commitments or contingent claims. Firm commitments include forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps involving a periodic exchange of cash flows and an option is the primary contingent claim.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Lee-02
entry.itemBody: Compared to over-the-counter derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives:

answerFeedback.621d2a80-ffdc-4eb8-a647-5e1c873e2b1e: Incorrect because OTC and ETD markets differ in several ways, including that ETD contracts are more standardized.
answerFeedback.6baa289a-aad9-440c-ab9b-63b008364810: Correct because OTC and ETD markets differ in several ways, including that ETD contracts have lower trading and transaction costs.
answerFeedback.f82e55ef-fb88-4d55-9a0e-3d816f32acea: Incorrect because OTC and ETD markets differ in several ways, including that OTC instruments have less transparency, whereas ETD markets have transparency.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Kashyap-05
entry.itemBody: Which of the following most likely has an embedded derivative in its structure?

answerFeedback.07d099c8-ee79-4a53-a2df-6e6930917074: Incorrect because a stand-alone derivative, is a distinct derivative contract, such as a derivative on a stock or bond. A put option is therefore a stand-alone derivative not an embedded derivative.
answerFeedback.4275a65c-8bd9-4840-a60e-0ab0326fb0e9: Correct because an embedded derivative is a derivative within an underlying, such as a callable, puttable, or convertible bond.
answerFeedback.bb9f63ce-f7de-4aec-b5d6-1e5bf0972738: Incorrect because a stand-alone derivative, is a distinct derivative contract, such as a derivative on a stock or bond. A futures contract is also a distinct derivative contract as it is not embedded in the underlying asset.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Kashyap-07
entry.itemBody: In the over-the-counter derivatives market, most transactions occur between end users and:

answerFeedback.4d78f3a2-0587-4f59-8657-1d755bc66b5e: Incorrect because end users do not generally trade with other end users. OTC derivative markets involve contracts entered between derivatives end users and dealers, or financial intermediaries, such as commercial banks or investment banks.
answerFeedback.ba21540b-658f-4692-9eeb-8e4b2aca9738: Incorrect because the central counterparty provides clearing and settlement functions rather than trading derivatives. A central counterparty (CCP) assumes the credit risk between derivative counterparties, one of which is typically a financial intermediary. CCPs provide clearing and settlement for most derivative contracts.
answerFeedback.bdb3fd25-2c4e-4394-88c5-dea5d513a20d: Correct because OTC (over-the-counter) derivative markets involve contracts entered between derivatives end users and dealers, or financial intermediaries, such as commercial banks or investment banks.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-Deriv-Kashyap-11
entry.itemBody: An end user seeking to hedge a specific underlying exposure having non-standard size and settlement dates would most likely trade on a(n):

answerFeedback.4dd1ab74-5380-4232-bf48-7e48b18b062c: Incorrect because ETD (exchange-traded derivative) contracts are more formal and standardized, which facilitates a more liquid and transparent market. Terms and conditions—such as the size of each contract, type, quality, and location of underlying for commodities and maturity date—are set by the exchange.
answerFeedback.54b050d2-5eb8-4857-8e78-afadf0ad7b4c: Incorrect because futures contracts are forward contracts with standardized sizes, dates, and underlyings that trade on futures exchanges. Therefore, they are inappropriate for the non-standard size and settlement dates required by the end user.
answerFeedback.567388e4-1375-40df-8191-3edef7c4f5cc: Correct because the terms of OTC (over-the-counter) contracts can be customized to match a desired risk exposure profile. This flexibility is important to end users seeking to hedge a specific existing or anticipated underlying exposure based upon non-standard terms.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.08-Deriv-Tyler-10
entry.itemBody:
The following portfolios contain a company's stock and a derivative on the stock:

Portfolio Securities
1 Stock and a short futures position
2 Stock and a short call option position
3 Stock and a short warrant position

The portfolio containing a derivative acting as a firm commitment to hedge the stock is most likely:

answerFeedback.00b9e2f3-8f41-4b17-90ae-7acef0e4f7a3: Correct because the buyer of a derivative enters a contract whose value changes in a way similar to a long position in the underlying. Thus a short futures position hedges the exposure to the underlying: Use of a derivative to offset or neutralize existing or anticipated exposure to an underlying is referred to as hedging, with the derivative itself commonly described as a hedge of the underlying transaction. In addition, a futures position is a firm commitment: Firm commitments include forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps involving a periodic exchange of cash flows.
answerFeedback.72872603-8a7c-433a-b0af-6b9c85cac533: Incorrect because a warrant is a type of option and an option is an example of a contingent claim rather than a firm commitment. Firm commitments include forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps involving a periodic exchange of cash flows. Another type of derivative is a contingent claim, in which one of the counterparties determines whether and when the trade will settle. An option is the primary contingent claim. Companies may also issue warrants, which are options granted to employees or sold to the public that allow holders to purchase shares at a fixed price in the future directly from the issuer.
answerFeedback.bfc76074-75ce-4c52-8af1-b77f7cd7d765: Incorrect because an option is an example of a contingent claim rather than a firm commitment. Firm commitments include forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps involving a periodic exchange of cash flows. Another type of derivative is a contingent claim, in which one of the counterparties determines whether and when the trade will settle. An option is the primary contingent claim.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q1
entry.itemBody: The short-term shutdown point of production for a firm operating under perfect competition will most likely occur when:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The firm should shut down production when marginal revenue is less than or equal to average variable cost.

choices.itemBody: A. price is equal to average total cost.
B. marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost.
C. marginal revenue is equal to average variable costs.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q2
entry.itemBody: Under conditions of perfect competition, a company will break even when market price is equal to the minimum point of the:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. A company is said to break even if its total revenue is equal to its total cost. Under conditions of perfect competition, a company will break even when market price is equal to the minimum point of the average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q3
entry.itemBody: A company will shut down production in the short run if total revenue is less than total:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A company will shut down production in the short run when total revenue is below total variable costs.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q4
entry.itemBody: A company has total variable costs of $4 million and fixed costs of $3 million. Based on this information, the company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue is at least:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. A company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue is equal to or greater than total cost. Because total costs are $7 million ($4 million variable costs and $3 million fixed costs), the company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue equals at least $7 million.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q5
entry.itemBody: When total revenue is greater than total variable costs but less than total costs, in the short term, a firm will most likely:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. When total revenue is enough to cover variable costs but not total fixed costs in full, the firm can survive in the short run but would not be able to maintain financial solvency in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q6
entry.itemBody: Under conditions of perfect competition, in the long run, firms will most likely earn:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Competition should drive prices down to long-run marginal cost, resulting in only normal profits being earned.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q7
entry.itemBody: A firm that increases its quantity produced without any change in per-unit cost is experiencing:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Output increases in the same proportion as input increases occur at constant returns to scale.

choices.itemBody: C. constant returns to scale. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 2 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q8
entry.itemBody: A company is experiencing economies of scale when:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Economies of scale occur if, as the firm increases output, cost per unit of production falls. Graphically, this definition translates into an LRAC with a negative slope.

choices.itemBody: A. cost per unit increases as output increases.
B. it is operating at a point on the LRAC curve at which the slope is negative.
C. it is operating beyond the minimum point on the long-run average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q9
entry.itemBody: Diseconomies of scale most likely result from:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. As the firm increases output, diseconomies of scale and higher average total costs can result when business functions and product lines overlap or are duplicated.

choices.itemBody: B. overlap of business functions and product lines.
C. discounted prices on resources when buying in larger quantities.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q10
entry.itemBody: A firm is operating beyond minimum efficient scale in a perfectly competitive industry. To maintain long-term viability, the most likely course of action for the firm is to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The firm operating at greater than long-run efficient scale is subject to diseconomies of scale. It should plan to decrease its level of production.

choices.itemBody: A. operate at the current level of production.
B. increase its level of production to gain economies of scale.
C. decrease its level of production to the minimum point on the long-run average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q11
entry.itemBody: Companies most likely have a well-defined supply function when the market structure is:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A company in a perfectly competitive market must accept whatever price the market dictates. The marginal cost schedule of a company in a perfectly competitive market determines its supply function.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q12
entry.itemBody: Aquarius, Inc. is the dominant company and the price leader in its market. One of the other companies in the market attempts to gain market share by undercutting the price set by Aquarius. The market share of Aquarius will most likely:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. As prices decrease, smaller companies will leave the market rather than sell below cost. The market share of Aquarius, the price leader, will increase. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 11 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q13
entry.itemBody: Over time, the market share of the dominant company in an oligopolistic market will most likely:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The dominant company’s market share tends to decrease as profits attract entry by other companies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q14
entry.itemBody: Successful advertising and product differentiation are most likely to have a positive impact on the economic profits of a producer under:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Advertising and product differentiation are most likely to have a positive impact on the economic profits of producers under monopolistic competition. The monopoly aspect of this structure arises from the ability to differentiate its product.

choices.itemBody: C. monopoly. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 3 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q15
entry.itemBody: The two dominant supermarket chains in the area are attempting to increase their market share by moving to 24-hour service instead of closing at 9 p.m. every night. The strategic outcomes and payoff matrix that arise from their actions are depicted in the diagram (with the shaded sections representing payoffs for Chain 2). The most likely Nash equilibrium strategy for the two chains is for:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Each company will consider the other’s reaction in selecting its strategy. Using the following summary, it is best for both chains to provide 24-hour service. Chain Consideration Best Decision If it opens for 24 hours, it will see a higher payoff regardless of what Chain 2 does. Chain 2 Chain 2 1 Closes at 9 p.m. Opens for 24 hours Open for 24 hours Chain 1 earns 540 instead of 180 Chain 1 earns 108 instead of 55 If it opens for 24 hours, it will see a higher payoff regardless of what Chain 1 does. Chain 1 Chain 1 2 Chain 1 Closes at 9 p.m. Chain 1 Opens for 24 hours Open for 24 hours Chain 2 earns 592 instead of 290 Chain 2 earns 140 instead of 75

choices.itemBody: A. both chains to open for 24 hours.
B. only Chain 2 to open for 24 hours.
C. both chains to close at 9 p.m.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q16
entry.itemBody: Six companies in an industry have the following market shares: Company A B C D E F Market Share (%) 30 25 16 12 10 7 If Companies D and F merge into a new Company, G, the industry’s three -company concentration ratio would be closest to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The concentration ratio for the top three companies would be 74%: A (30%) + B (25%) + G (12% + 7%).

choices.itemBody: C. 74%. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 4 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q17
entry.itemBody: Assume that two firms in a duopoly enter into a collusive agreement in an attempt to form a cartel and restrict output, raise prices, and increase profits. According to the Nash equilibrium, a low price is most likely charged by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The market outcomes for two firms in a duopoly is shown in the diagram. The lower left hand quadrant is the Nash solution when there is no collusion. However, with collusion, if ArcCo shares at least enough of its profit in the bottom right quadrant to provide BatCo more than it would receive in the lower left, it will be the optimal solution for the pair: the maximum joint profits will arise where both firms charge high prices for the product. entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q18

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The characteristics of monopolistic competition include a large number of competitors, low pricing power, and the production of differentiated products (through advertising and other non -price strategies), but these still result in some pricing power. The ease of entry results in zero economic profits in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q20
entry.itemBody: Three firms operate under perfect competition, producing 900 units of the same product but using different production technologies. Each company’s cost structure is indicated in the table: Company X Y Z Total Variable Costs $2,700 $3,600 $4,500 Total Fixed Costs 2,700 1,800 900 Total Costs $5,400 $5,400 $5,400 Which of the following statements is most accurate? If the unit selling price is:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Revenue–Cost Relationship Short-Run Decision Long-Term Decision TR ≥ TC Stay in market Stay in market TR > TVC but TR < TFC + TVC Stay in market Exit market TR < TVC Shut down production Exit market TR = Total Revenue; TC = Total Costs; TVC = Total Variable Costs; TFC = Total Fixed Costs Hence, if the selling price is $3.00, total revenue for all firms will be $3.00/unit × 900 units = $2,700. Only Firm X’s variable costs are covered and it should continue operating, while Firms Y and Z should immediately shut down production.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q21
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about a downward -sloping long -run average cost (LRAC) curve is most accurate? A downward -sloping LRAC curve is representative of a firm experiencing:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. When the LRAC curve is downward sloping, it means the firm is producing units at lower average costs per unit as production levels rise. This situation represents economies of scale in production.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q22
entry.itemBody: Firms operating under a monopolistic competition market structure most likely:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because under monopolistic competition, the products offered by each seller are close substitutes for the products offered by other firms, and each firm tries to make its product look different.

choices.itemBody: B. benefit from high barriers to entry.
C. sell products that are close substitutes for those offered by other firms.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q23
entry.itemBody: A market structure characterized by homogeneous/standardized product differentiation is best described as:

entry.itemBody: In a perfectly competitive market, a firm's breakeven point is the minimum point of the:

entry.itemBody: In the long run, a monopolistically competitive firm: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 6 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q26
entry.itemBody: In an oligopoly market, which of the following best describes the situation when firms have no incentive to deviate from their current pricing strategy based on the anticipated choices of competitors?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the Nash equilibrium is present when two or more participants in a non - cooperative game have no incentive to deviate from their respective equilibrium strategies after they have considered and anticipated their opponent’s rational choices or strategies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q27
entry.itemBody: In which of the following market structures does marginal revenue equal price?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because only in perfect competition does the marginal revenue equal price. In the remaining structures, price generally exceeds marginal revenue because a firm can sell more units only by reducing the per unit price.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q28
entry.itemBody: The perfectly competitive firm's supply curve is its long-run:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the long-run marginal cost schedule is the perfectly competitive firm's supply curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q29
entry.itemBody: To calculate the Herfindahl–Hirschman index:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because to avoid the known issues with concentration ratios, economists O.C. Herfindahl and A.O. Hirschman suggested an index where the market shares of the top N companies are first squared and then added.

choices.itemBody: A. add the market shares of the largest firms.
B. add the market shares of the largest firms and then square the sum.
C. square the market shares of the largest firms and then add the results.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q30
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information about three markets: Number of Sellers Non-Price Competition Market 1 Many None Market 2 Few Strong Market 3 Many Strong Which market is most likely an oligopoly?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in an oligopoly market there are a small number of potential sellers and products are often highly differentiated through marketing, features, and other non-price strategies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q31
entry.itemBody: Monopolistic competition is best characterized by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because for a monopolistically competitive firm: suppliers differentiate their products through advertising and other non-price strategies.

choices.itemBody: A. high barriers to entry and exit.
B. a small number of buyers and sellers.
C. product differentiation through non-price strategies. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 7 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q32
entry.itemBody: If a perfectly competitive industry becomes monopolistically competitive, each firm's long-run average total cost per unit sold will most likely:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because unlike long-run equilibrium in perfect competition, in the market of monopolistic competition, the equilibrium position is at a higher level of average cost than the level of output that minimizes average cost. Average cost does not reach its minim um until output level Q2 is achieved. Under perfect competition a product is produced at the efficient quantity (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) and average total cost is minimized. The demand faced by each firm is perfectly elastic (ho rizontal demand curve). However, under monopolistic competition the demand curve is downward sloping and the quantity produced (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) is not where average total cost is minimized. Thus, average total cost is lower under perfect competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q33
entry.itemBody: If a monopolistically competitive industry becomes perfectly competitive, each firm's long-run average total cost per unit sold will most likely:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because under perfect competition a product is produced at the efficient quantity (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) and the average total cost is Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 14 of 16 minimized. The demand curve faced by each firm is perfectly elastic (horizontal demand curve). However, under monopolistic competition the demand curve is downward sloping and the quantity produced (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) is not where average total cost is minimized. Thus, average total cost is lower under perfect competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q34
entry.itemBody: In the short run, the shutdown point of a company with a total variable cost of $3 million and a total fixed cost of $5 million is when total revenue declines to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because as long as the firm’s revenues cover at least its variable cost, the firm is better off continuing to operate. If price is greater than average variable cost (AVC), the firm is covering not only all of its variable cost but also a portion of fixed cost. Also, average revenue (AR) is revenue per unit.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q35
entry.itemBody: A firm in a market environment characterized by monopolistic competition is most likely to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. as the name implies, monopolistic competition is a hybrid market structure. The most distinctive factor in monopolistic competition is product differentiation. Although the market is made up of many firms that compose the product group, each producer attempt s to distinguish its product from that of the others, and product differentiation is accomplished in a variety of ways.

choices.itemBody: A. continue to experience economic profit in the long run.
B. have a well-defined supply function reflecting its marginal and average costs.
C. have many competitors each following its own product differentiation strategy.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q36
entry.itemBody: In long-run equilibrium, the perfectly competitive firm's supply curve is best represented by the firm's long-run:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the long-run marginal cost schedule is the perfectly competitive firm’s supply curve. The firm’s demand curve is dictated by the aggregate market’s equilibrium price. The basic rule of profit maximization is that MR = MC, as is the case in long-run equilibrium.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q37
entry.itemBody: Under monopolistic competition, a firm's supply curve is represented by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because in perfect competition, the firm’s supply schedule is represented by the marginal cost schedule. In monopolistic competition, there is no well -defined supply function. The information used to determine the appropriate level of output is based on the intersection of MC and MR. However, the price that will be charged is based on the market demand schedule. The firm’s supply curve should measure the quantity the firm is willing to supply at various prices. That information is not represented by either marginal cost or average cost.

choices.itemBody: C. neither average cost nor marginal cost.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q38
entry.itemBody: Under which of the following market structures are pricing strategies most likely influenced by the expected reaction of other firms?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the oligopoly market structure is based on a relatively small number of firms supplying the market. The small number of firms in the market means that each firm must consider what retaliatory strategies the other firms will pursue when prices and production levels change. Consider the pricing behavior of commercial airline companies. Pricing strategies and route scheduling are based on the expected reaction of the other carriers in similar markets.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q39
entry.itemBody: Each oligopoly firm faces an individual demand curve under: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 8 of 16

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in an oligopoly market where collusion is present, the aggregate market demand curve is divided up by the individual production participants. Under non-colluding market conditions, each firm faces an individual demand curve.

choices.itemBody: C. both colluding and non-colluding market conditions.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q40
entry.itemBody: In theory, under which of the following market structures do firms have the least control over price?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because from the perspective of the owners of the firm, the most desirable market structure is that with the most control over price, because this control can lead to large profits. Monopoly and oligopoly markets offer the greatest Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 15 of 16 potential control over price; monopolistic competition offers less control. Firms operating under perfectly competitive market conditions have no control over price.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q41
entry.itemBody: According to the Cournot assumption, in an oligopoly market each firm determines its profit-maximizing production level by assuming that other firms will:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in the Cournot assumption, each firm determines its profit - maximizing production level by assuming that the other firms' output will not change. This assumption simplifies pricing strategy because there is no need to guess what the other firm will do to retaliate.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q42
entry.itemBody: Which of the following indicators suggest(s) a monopoly market?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the concentration ratio is the sum of the market shares of the largest N firms. This number is always between zero (perfect competition) and 100 percent (monopoly).

choices.itemBody: B. A Herfindahl–Hirschman index of zero only
C. Both a concentration ratio of 100% and a Herfindahl–Hirschman index of zero

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q43
entry.itemBody: The Herfindahl–Hirschman index is calculated based on:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because in calculating the Herfindahl –Hirschman index the market shares of the top N companies are first squared and then added. If one firm controls the whole market (a monopoly), the Herfindahl –Hirschman index (HHI) equals 1. If there are M firms in the industry with equal market shares, then the HHI equals (1/M).

choices.itemBody: B. elasticity of demand in the market.
C. probability of new entry into the market.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q44
entry.itemBody: Which of the following market structures has high barriers to entry?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the characteristics of oligopoly markets include: entry into the market is difficult, with fairly high costs and significant barriers to competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q45
entry.itemBody: Under which of the following market structures is product differentiation most important?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because monopolistic competition is also highly competitive; however, it is considered a form of imperfect competition. The competitive characteristic is a notably large number of firms, while the monopoly aspect is the result of product differentiation. That is, if the seller can convince consumers that its product is uniquely different from other, similar products, then the seller can exercise some degree of pricing power over the market.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q46
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about a firm operating in a perfectly competitive market: Total variable costs 700 Total fixed costs 400 If the firm's total revenue is $1,000 million, the firm should: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 9 of 16

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because when TR total revenue is enough to cover TVC (total variable costs) but not all of TFC total fixed costs, the firm can continue to produce in the short run but will be unable to maintain financial solvency in the long run. TR is $1,000 which is greater than TVC of $700, but not enough to cover the firm's TFC of $400. Therefore, the firm will exit the market in the long run.

choices.itemBody: A. stay in the market in both the short run and long run.
B. stay in the market in the short run and exit the market in the long run.
C. shut down production in the short run and exit the market in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q47
entry.itemBody: A perfectly competitive market structure:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because profits under the conditions of perfect competition are driven to the required rate of return paid by the entrepreneur to borrow capital from investors (so-called normal profit or rental cost of capital).

choices.itemBody: B. causes all industries to ultimately fail due to lack of profits.
C. drives company profits to the investors' required rate of return.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q48
entry.itemBody: In the short run, a firm most likely shuts down production when:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because the firm must cover its variable cost to remain in business in the short run. If TR cannot cover TVC, the firm shuts down production to minimize loss. The loss would be equal to the amount of fixed cost.

choices.itemBody: B. sunk costs are greater than total revenue.
C. total revenue is less than total variable cost.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q49
entry.itemBody: A disadvantage of the concentration ratio is that it:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because a disadvantage of the concentration ratio is that it tends to be unaffected by mergers among the top market incumbents. For example, if the largest and second-largest incumbents merge, the pricing power of the combined entity is Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 16 of 16 likely to be larger than that of the two pre-existing companies. But the concentration ratio may not change much.

choices.itemBody: A. requires a large number of time-series observations.
B. is largely unaffected by mergers among the top market incumbents.
C. requires the specification of the explanatory variables used in regression analysis.

entry.title: 2027-Mod66-Q50
entry.itemBody: A manufacturing company expanded in a new region by setting up local assembly lines and hiring local staff. Two years later, the company's sale had grown as expected but operating margin had shrunk from 15 to 12 percent. The company:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the company is most likely suffering from diseconomies of scale. It is having to duplicate all costs in each location, and by targeting different demographics, it has added additional costs for inputs and marketing. Therefore, the company’s fixed costs have increased faster than output, and the economic result is diseconomies of scale.

choices.itemBody: A. has yet to reach its breakeven volume.
B. is suffering from diseconomies of scale.
